clue.text: Male relatives, American, in the US itself

explanation.surface: A family tree note about American uncles living in the States.
explanation.walkthrough: Uncle Sam is the cartoon figure in a top hat who personifies the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: The bearded figure is a national personification, standing for the American government and country as a whole.

clue.text: Doorkeeper has no heroin for a drug addict

indicators.note: 'has no' says the word lacks something, so a letter is taken out

parts.note: an usher shows people in at the door
H is slang for heroin; this is the letter removed

explanation.surface: A doorman has no heroin to sell to an addict.
explanation.definitionFit: A user is drug slang for someone who takes drugs regularly, an addict.

clue.text: Be contrary to ordinary procedure, and include many different groups

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to go against normal practice
second meaning: to affect or span several categories, as an issue cutting across party lines

explanation.walkthrough: Both senses use the picture of a line drawn over others: cutting across the usual rules, or across group boundaries.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to run counter to established practice and to extend over many divisions.

clue.text: Football team, until now, not expected to be promoted

parts.note: ever as in 'the best ever', meaning up to the present

indicators.note: in a down entry, something promoted moves up, so the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: taken as written, then turned upwards

explanation.surface: A football club that has never been tipped for promotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Promoted' sounds like football league talk, but in a down clue it means reading upwards. Everton is a Premier League club from Liverpool.
explanation.definitionFit: Everton is the name of a long-established English professional football club.

clue.text: Very quickly, tenor brought in two articles on twin

indicators.note: something brought in is placed inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: the indefinite article and the definite article
T is the abbreviation for tenor
a double is an exact likeness, like a twin

explanation.surface: A tenor is rushed in to sing two pieces alongside his twin.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a military command for marching at double time, hence very fast.

clue.text: Trim a tree

definitions.meaning: first meaning: neat and smart in appearance

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as an instruction to prune a tree, but 'Trim' is the adjective meaning neat.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an adjective for a smart, tidy appearance and the name of a common conifer.

clue.text: Talk foolishly about the Spanish Church dignitary

indicators.note: 'about' means surrounding, so the first word goes around the next piece

parts.note: to prate is to chatter idly
el is the Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Someone babbles nonsense about a Spanish bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: A prelate is a high-ranking member of the clergy, such as a bishop or archbishop.

clue.text: A French article, one on marriage

explanation.surface: A French newspaper piece on the subject of marriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' suggests a piece of writing; it is the grammatical word for 'a'.
explanation.definitionFit: A union is a joining of two people in wedlock, another word for marriage.

clue.text: Simple female rabbit, ahead of rest, must be careful

parts.note: a doe is a female rabbit or deer

explanation.surface: A plain-minded doe rabbit in front of the others should take care.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a spoken warning to proceed slowly and carefully, saying one must take care.

clue.text: Appeal of centre, at York

indicators.note: 'of' marks the answer as made out of part of the following words, sitting inside them

parts.note: runs from just after the first letter of centre to the first letter of York

explanation.surface: An appeal made by a centre in the city of York.
explanation.definitionFit: An entreaty is an earnest request or plea, which is what an appeal is.

clue.text: Thoughtless concerning young lady

parts.note: a miss is a girl or young woman

explanation.surface: Someone is being careless with regard to a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Remiss means negligent or careless in one's duty, close in sense to thoughtless.

clue.text: Thoughtless broadcast knocked on the head

parts.note: to broadcast seed is to scatter it
to brain someone is to hit them on the head

explanation.surface: A careless radio or TV programme that got its presenter hit on the head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' suggests radio, but here it is the older farming verb for sowing seed widely.
explanation.definitionFit: A scatterbrained person is disorganised and forgetful, lacking careful thought.

clue.text: Drat, another obit misprinted

indicators.note: a misprint puts letters in the wrong places, so these are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor swears as yet another obituary comes out with errors.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild exclamations of annoyance, interchangeable as expletives.

clue.text: Short walk to meet nun, a relation

parts.note: a step is a very short walk
a nun is addressed as Sister

explanation.surface: Taking a brief stroll to meet a nun who is a family member.
explanation.definitionFit: A stepsister is related by a parent's remarriage, so she is a relation.

clue.text: Terribly hot service, a source of irritation

indicators.note: something done terribly is done badly, so the following letters come out jumbled

parts.note: the Royal Navy is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: A tennis serve or church service in the heat proves irritating.
explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords 'service' often means one of the armed forces: RN is the Royal Navy.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorn in one's side is a persistent annoyance, so a thorn is a source of irritation.

clue.text: Honest one managed to win

indicators.note: letters that are managed are handled and organised into a new order

explanation.surface: A fair-dealing person succeeded in winning.
explanation.walkthrough: In horse-race betting, a bet placed on the nose is a bet that the horse will finish first, not merely place.
explanation.definitionFit: Betting slang: money staked on the nose pays only if the horse wins outright.

clue.text: Stubborn, old boy, say, round home

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

indicators.note: 'round' means surrounding, so the word before goes around the next piece

explanation.surface: A pig-headed former pupil, for example, at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' looks like 'for example' but is the verb, state.
explanation.definitionFit: Obstinate means refusing to change one's mind, a close synonym of stubborn.

clue.text: What may have been done on the dance floor — pals booed off

definitions.text: What may have been done on the dance floor

indicators.note: 'off' suggests going wrong or out of order, so the preceding letters are disturbed

explanation.surface: A dance-floor performance so bad that friends booed the dancers off.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a cryptic description; it fits any dance, and the anagram pins down which.
explanation.definitionFit: The paso doble is a fast Latin ballroom dance modelled on a bullfight march, so it is performed on a dance floor.

clue.text: New editor on tabloid, initially from a city in Michigan

indicators.note: something new is made afresh, so the letters following are set in a fresh order
'initially' asks for the first letter of the word just before it

explanation.surface: A newly appointed tabloid editor comes from Michigan.
explanation.definitionFit: Detroit is the largest city in the US state of Michigan, home of the American car industry.

clue.text: Dish from Tarsus, historically

indicators.note: 'from' says the answer is taken out of the run of letters that follows

parts.note: the end of the city name plus the start of the adverb

explanation.surface: A traditional dish of the ancient city of Tarsus.
explanation.walkthrough: Tarsus is a city in southern Turkey, known as the birthplace of St Paul.
explanation.definitionFit: Sushi is a Japanese dish of vinegared rice with raw fish, so it is a dish.

clue.text: Part of street housing e.g. soldiers

indicators.note: a building housing people holds them inside, so the outer word goes around the rest

parts.note: soldiers are men in the ranks

explanation.surface: A part of a street where soldiers, for instance, are billeted.
explanation.definitionFit: A segment is one of the sections into which a whole is divided, so it is a part.

clue.text: Also at home, young child, male, by arrangement

parts.note: a bargain is a deal or agreement

explanation.surface: Also present at home: a toddler, a man, by some arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By arrangement' reads like an anagram signal, but there is nothing to rearrange; arrangement is the agreement itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in addition or as well, so it can replace the adverb also.

clue.text: Pound, peppered broth

indicators.note: something peppered is sprinkled about, so the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: A pound of seasoned soup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pound' tempts as a weight or currency; it is the verb, to beat.
explanation.definitionFit: To throb is to beat with a strong, regular rhythm, as a heart pounds.

clue.text: Put money on a Greek character

parts.note: to bet is to wager money

explanation.surface: Placing a wager on a Greek person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' suggests a person; here it is a letter of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Beta is the second letter of the Greek alphabet, so it is a Greek written character.

clue.text: Fish, trout, baked — entertaining starter in bistro

indicators.note: something baked is cooked and transformed, so the word before is jumbled
to entertain a guest is to take them in, so one part holds the other
the starter of a meal comes first, so only the opening letter of the next word counts

explanation.surface: A bistro menu: baked trout, with something to entertain diners before it.
explanation.walkthrough: Trout looks like the fish being defined, but it is the anagram fodder; the definition is the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: The turbot is a large European flatfish prized for eating, so it is an example of a fish.

clue.text: Terrier shown by porter

parts.note: a programme that has aired has been shown
porter is a dark beer, a kind of ale

explanation.surface: A dog exhibited at a show by a hotel porter.
explanation.walkthrough: The porter seems to be the person showing the dog; here it is the drink. 'By' places the beer after the first part.
explanation.definitionFit: The Airedale is the largest breed of terrier, named after a valley in Yorkshire.

clue.text: Take place over in desert? First to expect money back

indicators.note: 'in' places one piece inside another

parts.note: to rat on someone is to desert them

indicators.note: turned over means flipped round, so the phrase before is read backwards

parts.note: to be is to happen or take place; turned round

indicators.note: 'first' asks only for the opening letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Holding an event in the desert, you should first expect a refund.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desert' looks like a noun, a sandy place, but it is the verb, abandon.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebate is a partial refund, an amount of money paid back.

clue.text: Song about a leader in Asia is abhorrent

definitions.note: the answer is a noun used predicatively, as in 'it is anathema to me'

indicators.note: 'about' means around, so the first word wraps the next piece

parts.note: an anthem is a song of praise or a national song

indicators.note: the leader goes first, so only the opening letter of the next word is used

explanation.surface: A national song honouring an Asian leader is found offensive.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is anathema is detested or loathed, which is what abhorrent describes.
